summary: Source decomposition of the abstract completed-cohomology machinery from Calegari-Emerton's survey, read in full for its statements, together with Scholze's section 4.2 for the perfectoid comparison and the vanishing and codimension results it yields. Covered with nodes: the tower axioms and the two standing hypotheses (finite simplicial homotopy type, p-adic analytic G_0) that the source says are not removable; the four completed modules and the exact sequence separating the p-adic completion from the Tate module; finite generation over the Iwasawa algebra with the identification of the canonical and projective-limit topologies; the duality sequences (exact in characteristic zero, isomorphisms mod p) and the universal-coefficient sequences; the Hochschild-Serre descent spectral sequences; codimension and Iwasawa dimension with the torsion theorem; the Borel-Serre boundary tower; and Scholze's named comparison isomorphism with its tame-level convention. The dominant boundary is that the survey PROVES none of its main theorems: Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 1.16 are deferred to a paper that is not in the supplied library. Conjecture 1.5 is recorded as a conjecture, not an input.

nodes.title: The axioms on the tower, and the two standing hypotheses without which nothing is controlled
nodes.statement: Let G_0 be a profinite group with a countable basis of neighbourhoods of the identity consisting of normal open subgroups ... contained in G_r contained in ... contained in G_1 contained in G_0. Suppose given a tower of topological spaces ... -> X_r -> ... -> X_1 -> X_0, each with an action of G_0, such that (1) the maps X_{r+1} -> X_r are G_0-equivariant, and (2) G_r acts trivially on X_r and realizes X_r as a G_0/G_r-torsor over X_0 - in particular all the maps in the tower are FINITE COVERINGS. Two standing hypotheses are imposed from that point on: (a) each X_r is a manifold homotopic to a finite simplicial complex, which is what makes all four families of (co)homology groups finitely generated over the indicated coefficient ring and relates them by the appropriate duality; and (b) G_0 is a p-ADIC ANALYTIC group - the source says that without this 'it seems impossible to control the inverse limits involved in our constructions', and with it Lazard's theorem that Z_p[[G_0]] is noetherian plus Schneider-Teitelbaum's Banach-representation theory bring the limits under control. In the arithmetic application X_r = G(Q)\G(A)/A_infinity^o K_infinity^o G_r K^{infinity,p}, and the resulting modules carry not only the G_0-action but actions of the whole p-adic group G(Q_p), of a completed Hecke algebra T built from spherical Hecke operators at primes l different from p where G and the tame level K^{infinity,p} are unramified, and of the component group pi_0 = (A_infinity K_infinity)/(A_infinity^o K_infinity^o).
hypotheses: the tower must consist of FINITE coverings with G_r acting trivially on X_r; without the torsor condition the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequences of Theorem 1.1(4) do not exist
each X_r homotopic to a FINITE simplicial complex: this is what gives finite generation at each level

proofSteps: The source lays out the axioms, then imposes the two standing hypotheses with explicit reasons.
It notes in a footnote that a companion paper gives a sheaf-theoretic description of the completed cohomology allowing a more flexible set-up, which it does not need.

nodes.title: The four completed (co)homology modules, and the exact sequence separating the completion from the Tate module
nodes.statement: Having fixed p, define completed homology and cohomology by H-tilde_bullet = inverse limit over r of H_bullet(X_r, Z_p) and H-tilde^bullet = inverse limit over s of the direct limit over r of H^bullet(X_r, Z/p^s Z), with Borel-Moore and compactly supported variants H-tilde^BM_bullet = inverse limit over r of H^BM_bullet(X_r, Z_p) and H-tilde_c^bullet = inverse limit over s of the direct limit over r of H_c^bullet(X_r, Z/p^s Z). There are natural maps H-tilde_bullet -> H-tilde^BM_bullet and H-tilde_c^bullet -> H-tilde^bullet. Define also H-hat^bullet = the p-adic completion of the direct limit over r of H^bullet(X_r, Z_p), and T_p H^bullet = the p-adic Tate module of that direct limit. Then there is an exact sequence 0 -> H-hat^bullet -> H-tilde^bullet -> T_p H^{bullet+1} -> 0. The p-adic completion kills the p-divisible part of the direct limit, while the Tate module sees only the torsion subgroup of that divisible part. Since T_p H^{bullet+1} is p-torsion free and p-adically complete, dualizing gives 0 -> Hom(T_p H^{bullet+1}, Z_p) -> Hom(H-tilde^bullet, Z_p) -> Hom(H-hat^bullet, Z_p) -> 0, and by Theorem 1.1(3) the middle term is the p-torsion-free quotient of H-tilde_bullet.
hypotheses: the order of the limits is not interchangeable: H-tilde^bullet is inverse limit over s of direct limit over r, and the two other objects H-hat and T_p H are obtained from the SAME direct limit by completion and by Tate module respectively

the exact sequence is a consequence of the definitions, not a formal commutation of completion with cohomology; the stage text's demand to 'exhibit the possible lim^1 term rather than commuting completion and cohomology formally' is the same point
the dual sequence uses that T_p H^{bullet+1} is p-torsion free AND p-adically complete
proofSteps: The source gives the definitions and then the exact sequence (1.1) with the interpretation of its two outer terms.
Dualizing (1.1) over Z_p and quoting Theorem 1.1(3) identifies Hom(H-tilde^bullet, Z_p) with the p-torsion-free quotient of completed homology.

nodes.title: Theorem 1.1(1): finite generation of completed homology over Z_p[[G_0]], and the identification of two topologies
nodes.statement: Theorem 1.1(1): the natural action of Z_p[[G_0]] on H-tilde_bullet and on H-tilde^BM_bullet makes each of them a FINITELY GENERATED LEFT module over Z_p[[G_0]]; moreover the canonical topology on each (obtained by writing it as a quotient of a finite direct sum of copies of Z_p[[G_0]]) coincides with the projective limit topology. Consequence stated in the source: each torsion submodule H-tilde_bullet[p^infinity] and H-tilde^BM_bullet[p^infinity] is finitely generated over Z_p[[G_0]] and hence of BOUNDED EXPONENT. Mod p analogue, Theorem 1.16(1): F_p[[G_0]] acts on H-tilde_{bullet, F_p} and H-tilde^BM_{bullet, F_p} making each a finitely generated left module, again with the canonical topology equal to the projective limit topology; and Theorem 1.16(2): H^bullet_{F_p} and H^bullet_{c, F_p} are ADMISSIBLE SMOOTH representations of G_0 over F_p.

the source states that the PROOF of Theorem 1.1 'will appear in [6]' - the survey does not prove it
finite generation is not freeness, projectivity or Cohen-Macaulayness; the source draws only the bounded-exponent consequence
proofSteps: The source states Theorem 1.1 and attributes its proof to a forthcoming paper, noting that it strengthens earlier results by dealing explicitly with homology and with integral aspects rather than only after tensoring with Q_p.
Theorem 1.16 is the mod p analogue, also with proof deferred to the same forthcoming paper.

nodes.title: Theorem 1.1(3) and Theorem 1.16(3),(5): the exact sequences and isomorphisms relating completed homology and cohomology
nodes.statement: Theorem 1.1(3): there are short exact sequences 0 -> Hom_cont(H-tilde_{bullet-1}, Q_p/Z_p) -> H-tilde^bullet -> Hom_cont(H-tilde_bullet, Z_p) -> 0, where 'cont' means continuous for the canonical topology on the source and the evident (discrete or p-adic) topology on the target, and 0 -> Hom(H-tilde^{bullet+1}[p^infinity], Q_p/Z_p) -> H-tilde_bullet -> Hom(H-tilde^bullet, Z_p) -> 0, together with similar sequences relating H-tilde^BM_bullet and H-tilde_c^bullet; these are compatible with the maps H-tilde_bullet -> H-tilde^BM_bullet and H-tilde_c^bullet -> H-tilde^bullet. In the mod p setting the corresponding statements are ISOMORPHISMS, Theorem 1.16(3): H^bullet_{F_p} = Hom_cont(H-tilde_{bullet, F_p}, F_p) and H-tilde_{bullet, F_p} = Hom(H^bullet_{F_p}, F_p), again compatible with the Borel-Moore and compactly supported variants; and Theorem 1.16(5) gives the universal-coefficient sequences 0 -> H-tilde_bullet/p H-tilde_bullet -> H-tilde_{bullet, F_p} -> H-tilde_{bullet-1}[p] -> 0 and 0 -> H-tilde^bullet/p H-tilde^bullet -> H^bullet_{F_p} -> H-tilde^{bullet+1}[p] -> 0.
hypotheses: in characteristic zero duality is only an EXACT SEQUENCE with a torsion correction term, not an isomorphism; only mod p does it become an isomorphism

the continuity condition is with respect to the canonical topology on the source; the source remarks that on the cohomology side no continuity condition is needed because the natural topology there is p-adic and all Z_p-linear maps are automatically p-adically continuous
the correction terms shift the degree: Hom_cont(H-tilde_{bullet-1}, Q_p/Z_p) in one sequence and Hom(H-tilde^{bullet+1}[p^infinity], Q_p/Z_p) in the other

nodes.title: Theorem 1.1(4) and Theorem 1.16(4): the descent spectral sequences recovering finite-level cohomology
nodes.statement: Theorem 1.1(4): for each r >= 0 there are Hochschild-Serre type spectral sequences E_2^{i,j} = H^i(G_r, H-tilde^j) => H^{i+j}(X_r, Z_p) and E_2^{i,j} = H^i(G_r, H-tilde_c^j) => H_c^{i+j}(X_r, Z_p), compatible with the map H-tilde_c^bullet -> H-tilde^bullet. Theorem 1.16(4) is the mod p analogue with H^bullet_{F_p} and F_p coefficients on the abutment. Remark 1.2: if M is any continuous G_0-module over Z_p, one may associate a family of local systems M_bullet on the tower, and there is an analogue of part (4) for the cohomology of the local system M_r. This is the descent statement that recovers finite-level cohomology from the completed object; it is a SPECTRAL SEQUENCE, so the degree-zero invariants recover only the edge term.

the abutment is the Z_p-cohomology of X_r, not of its Borel-Serre compactification; the boundary is a separate long exact sequence
Remark 1.2's extension to arbitrary continuous coefficients M is stated without proof
the source does not claim that H^0(G_r, H-tilde^j) recovers classical forms; only the spectral sequence is asserted

nodes.title: Codimension over a noncommutative Iwasawa algebra, and Theorem 1.4: completed homology is torsion outside the middle degree
nodes.statement: For a finitely generated left Z_p[[G_0]]-module M set E^bullet(M) = Ext^bullet(M, Z_p[[G_0]]), computed via the left module structure on Z_p[[G_0]] and converted back to a left module structure by the canonical anti-involution g -> g^{-1}; these modules are unchanged (up to natural isomorphism and forgetting) on replacing G_0 by an open subgroup. The CODIMENSION of M is the least i with E^i(M) nonzero; the IWASAWA DIMENSION is 1 + dim G_0 - codim M. In the mod p setting E_{F_p}^bullet(M) = Ext^bullet(M, F_p[[G_0]]) and the short exact sequences 0 -> E^bullet(M) -> E_{F_p}^bullet(M) -> E^{bullet+1}(M) -> 0 show the F_p-codimension is one less than the codimension, so the Iwasawa dimension equals dim G_0 - codim_{F_p} M. Lemma 1.17: if M is finitely generated over Z_p[[G_0]] and p-TORSION FREE then codim M = codim_{F_p} M/pM. Theorem 1.4 (the main result of an earlier paper of the authors): if G is SEMI-SIMPLE then the modules H-tilde_n are TORSION Z_p[[G_0]]-modules, unless G(R) admits discrete series and n is the middle dimension (half the dimension of the X_r); in that case Hom(H-hat^n, Z_p), and hence H-tilde_n, has positive rank, while Hom(T_p H^{n+1}, Z_p) is torsion over Z_p[[G_0]]. Theorem 1.18: if M is finitely generated over F_p[[G_0]] with V = Hom_cont(M, F_p) the corresponding admissible smooth representation, and the Iwasawa dimension of M is d, then dim H^0(G_r, V) is asymptotic to lambda [G_0 : G_r]^{d/dim G_0} for some lambda > 0, while dim H^i(G_r, V) = O([G_0 : G_r]^{d/dim G_0}) for all i > 0.
hypotheses: codimension is defined only for FINITELY GENERATED modules over the completed group ring; it depends on G_0 only through an open subgroup
Theorem 1.4 assumes G SEMI-SIMPLE and its statement changes exactly when G(R) admits discrete series and n is the middle dimension

the source notes that the assertion about T_p H^{n+1} being torsion in the discrete-series middle dimension is not stated in the earlier paper but follows from its proof - an input that must be re-derived, not cited

nodes.title: The Borel-Serre boundary tower and its long exact sequences
nodes.statement: Each X_r embeds as an open subset of its Borel-Serre compactification X-bar_r; write dX_r = X-bar_r minus X_r for the boundary. As r varies the X-bar_r form a tower to which the completed (co)homology machinery applies, so one may define completed (co)homology spaces H-tilde_bullet(d) and H-tilde^bullet(d) of the boundary, and there are long exact sequences relating them to the interior and compactly supported objects. Scholze's Corollary 4.2.2, for the compactly supported completed cohomology of a Shimura variety of Hodge type with tame level K^p contained in the level-N subgroup for some N >= 3 prime to p: the group H-tilde^i_{c, K^p}(Z/p^n Z) (and a fortiori with Z_p coefficients) VANISHES for i > d, where d = dim_C X_K. Corollary 4.2.3: for i > d one has H-tilde^{BM}_i = 0 and H-tilde^{BM}_d is p-torsion free; for i < d the codimension of H-tilde_i over the Iwasawa algebra is at least d - i. If the X_K are compact this gives all of the Calegari-Emerton Conjecture 1.5 in that case, except with non-strict instead of strict inequalities on the codimensions (there l_0 = d and q_0 = 0).
hypotheses: the boundary construction needs the Borel-Serre compactification of each X_r and the compatibility of the compactifications along the tower

Scholze's results are for Shimura varieties of HODGE type, with a fixed embedding into a Siegel datum, and with the tame level convention K^p contained in the level-N subgroup of G'(A_f^p) for some N >= 3 prime to p
Corollary 4.2.3's comparison with Conjecture 1.5 holds with NON-STRICT inequalities and only when the X_K are compact

the proof of Corollary 4.2.2 is a statement about the cohomological dimension of a spectral space, and passes through the perfectoid/adic space at infinite level; it is not an argument about the archimedean tower
proofSteps: The survey records the boundary tower and its long exact sequences.

Scholze's Corollary 4.2.2 reduces to n = 1 by long exact sequences, then to showing that H-tilde^i_{c,K^p}(F_p) tensor O_C/p is almost zero for i > d, then by his Theorem 4.2.1 to the vanishing of H^i(X^*_{K^p}, F) for i > d for ANY abelian sheaf F on the spectral space X^*_{K^p}; that follows because a cofiltered inverse limit of spectral spaces of cohomological dimension at most d again has cohomological dimension at most d, and each finite-level adic space has cohomological dimension at most d.

Corollary 4.2.3's first two assertions follow from Corollary 4.2.2 together with Theorem 1.1(iii) of the survey; the codimension bound is proved by a minimal-counterexample argument using the Poincare duality spectral sequence E_2^{jk} = E^j(H-tilde_k) => H-tilde^{BM}_{2d-j-k}.

nodes.title: The convention of Scholze's section 4.2 and its comparison isomorphism
nodes.statement: In Scholze's section 4.2 the compactly supported completed cohomology used is H-tilde^i_{c,K^p}(Z/p^n Z) = direct limit over K_p of H^i_c(X_{K_p K^p}, Z/p^n Z), with (G, D) of Hodge type, a fixed embedding into (Sp_{2g}, D_{Sp_{2g}}), and the standing convention that the tame level K^p is contained in the level-N subgroup of G'(A_f^p) for some N >= 3 prime to p. Theorem 4.2.1: there is a natural isomorphism of almost-O_C-modules H-tilde^i_{c,K^p}(Z/p^n Z) tensor_{Z/p^n Z} O_C^a/p^n = H^i(X^*_{K^p}, I^{+a}_{X^*_{K^p}}/p^n), where the right-hand cohomology is computed on the topological space X^*_{K^p} and I_{X^*_{K^p}} is the ideal sheaf of the boundary with I^+ its intersection with O^+; moreover the isomorphism is compatible with the transition maps for K_1^p contained in K_2^p. This is the named comparison that identifies the abstract completed object with the perfectoid Shimura-tower model, and it is the convention (support and lattice) that the stage asks to compare against.
hypotheses: only the COMPACTLY SUPPORTED completed cohomology is compared; the statement is not about H-tilde^bullet
the comparison is an isomorphism of ALMOST O_C-modules, not of O_C-modules; the almost mathematics is not decoration
the tame level convention N >= 3 prime to p is imposed so that the finite levels are fine moduli problems
(G, D) must be of Hodge type with a chosen Siegel embedding; the statement is not available for arbitrary locally symmetric spaces
the right-hand side is the cohomology of the ideal sheaf of the BOUNDARY intersected with O^+, i.e. it carries the compact-support condition geometrically
